See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Median = middle sorted score; population SD = √[Σ(score − mean)² ÷ n]

A worked example

The grades 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 have a median and mean of 80%. Their range is 40 percentage points and their population standard deviation is approximately 14.14 points.

Before you use the result

This summary treats all entered scores as the full population and weights them equally. It does not calculate sample standard deviation, decide a curve or assign passing grades. Population standard deviation uses n in the denominator; a sample estimate typically uses n − 1. Up to 1,000 scores are accepted.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

What happens with an even number of grades?

The median is the mean of the two middle sorted values.

Does standard deviation show whether my class did well?

It measures spread, not academic quality or fairness. Interpret it with assessment context and the actual grading policy.
